newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks gain after data, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks gain after data, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: U.S. stocks drove higher in morning trading on Wednesday, tracking the bond market up after the release of data showing a 6.1 percent rise in new home sales for June, which was seen as stable for the economy.
The Dow Jones Industrial average gained 54 points, or 0.67 percent, to 8230. Its speedy climb prompted the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on index-arbitrage trading at 1010 EDT/1410 GMT.
The Nasdaq composite rose eight points to 1580.
The long bond was robust, up 22/32 to a 6.34 percent yield after the data.

"The data was as expected or slightly weaker," Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics, said. "The run rate is sort of on the soft side without being catastrophically weak...The bond market just wants to go up."

The U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes, seasonally adjusted, rose 6.1 percent to a 819,000 unit annual rate. May new home sales were revised down to a one percent increase from a 7.1 percent gain.
"There was a huge revision to last month," Ellis said.
This week, markets will also face the July employment report, due on Friday.
